title: CyberShield360
subtitle: From an exposed asset to an actionable finding.
introduction: I designed the architecture and security workflow for an attack surface management product, and helped take it to launch.

stages.label: Discover
stages.title: Make the external footprint visible.
stages.description: Bring domains, IP addresses, and exposed services into a view that a security team can investigate.
stages.decision: Start with a defined assessment scope and make discovery repeatable as the environment changes.
stages.output: An inventory of assets to assess
stages.diagram_label: Illustrative asset map connecting example.com to a web application, an API, and an IP address.

stages.label: Enrich
stages.title: Add context to every observation.
stages.description: Connect each asset to service information and relevant vulnerability data so an analyst has a useful starting point.
stages.decision: Keep a version match distinct from evidence of exploitability. Correlation starts an investigation.
stages.diagram_label: Illustrative evidence record for api.example.com, combining an observed HTTPS service, service identification, and a vulnerability correlation that needs validation.

stages.label: Prioritize
stages.title: Turn signals into a risk decision.
stages.description: Use exposure, supporting evidence, and the affected service to decide which findings deserve investigation first.
stages.decision: Give the security team the context behind a priority, with uncertainty visible alongside the finding.
stages.diagram_label: Illustrative prioritization flow: exposure, evidence, and service context feed an analyst review, which produces an investigation priority.

stages.label: Report
stages.title: Give engineering enough to act.
stages.description: Present the affected asset, supporting evidence, and remediation context in a report the responsible team can use.
stages.decision: Design the output around the next engineering action, making the finding understandable beyond the security team.
stages.output: A finding ready for remediation triage
stages.diagram_label: Illustrative report handoff with an affected asset, evidence, responsible team, and remediation next step.

ownership.label: My ownership
ownership.text: Product architecture, security design, and the discovery-to-reporting workflow.

ownership.label: Design trade-off
ownership.text: Broad discovery needed validation and context to become useful signal.

ownership.label: Shipped result
ownership.text: A launched product, introduced in Invia’s public launch videos.

tour.heading: 01 / Discover the external footprint
tour.caption: Start with the assessment scope. Bring domains, IP addresses, and exposed services into an inventory the security team can investigate.

tour.heading: 02 / Add evidence and context
tour.caption: Attach service information and relevant vulnerability data. A version match is a lead for investigation; exploitability still needs validation.

tour.heading: 03 / Decide what to investigate first
tour.caption: Consider exposure, supporting evidence, and the affected service together. Keep uncertainty visible so the team understands the priority.

tour.heading: 04 / Make the next action clear
tour.caption: Carry the affected asset, evidence, and remediation context into the report. Give the responsible engineering team enough information to act.

tour.heading: From security assessment to product ownership
tour.caption: At Invia, I owned product architecture and security design, defined the discovery and analysis pipeline, and helped take CyberShield360 to launch.
